rationale: shared.state defines storage, references and the allocation counter, shared.syntax defines statements and Delta, and shared.resolution/shared.give define route resolution and give cases. This unit introduces configurations and the statement-step judgment before using execution or stuckness. Configuration.initial pairs State.empty with program.body; finished is exactly an empty code list. Step.letValue runs Eval, checks destination absence in the evaluated variable table, binds its result, and retains precisely rest. Eval.give uses Give; Eval.giveShare replaces only the result mode; Eval.new requires a declared class, EvalArgs, equal field/result lengths, and a fresh identity at the evaluated counter. EvalArgs.nil/cons define left-to-right evaluation, and allocate zips results into declaration-order fields before incrementing the counter. Thus nested argument evaluations remain inside one machine transition. Supporting WellFormedWith accounts for temporary result owners rather than silently losing them from storage. Steps is reflexive/transitive finite execution; Stuck requires noncompletion and absence of every successor. Repeated unique giving fails under the distinct-slot convention already stated in shared.state, whereas shared giving leaves a reference available.
